p.i: Legio. Nam dæmonia multa ingressa erant in ips[?]um.

Beelzebub, Matth. 12. vers. 24.5
Diabolus, Matth. 25. v. 41. Iohan. 8. v. 44. 1. Iohan. 3. v. 8. Apoc. 12. v. 9. Eph. 6. v. 11. Iac. 4. v. 7.

ὁ πειράζων[?], id est, tentator, Matth. 4. vers. 3. 1. Thess. 3. vers. 5.10
Princeps mundi, Iohan. 12. vers. 31.
Draco magnus, Apoc. 12. v. 9.
Serpens antiquus, ibid.
Deus huius seculi, 2. Cor. 4. v. 4.15
Aduersarius fidelium, 1. Petri 5. v. 8.
Accusator fidelium, Apoc. 12. v. 10.
13. Mali angeli sunt tales affectu & effectu.
Hoc testantur ipsorum nomina, quibus appellantur,20 Spiritus mali, 1. Sam. 16. v. 15.
Sehirim, id est, horridi, Ier. 17. v. 7.
Schedim, id est, vastatores, Deut. 32. v. 17.
Spiritus immundi, Matth. 10. v. 1.
Principatus, potestates, domini mundi, rectores tenebrarum seculi huius, spirituales malitiæ, seu spiritus nequam, Eph. 6. vers. 12.25 Vide etiam num. praeced.
14. Angeli mali ex inferno emittuntur, ad castigandum & exercendum pios, & seducendum atque vexandum impios.30
1. Petri 2. vers. 4. Deus angelis, qui peccauerunt, non pepercit, sed in tartarum detrusos catenis caliginis tradidit, damnationi seruatos. Vide Iudæ vers. 6. ad num. 10.
1. Sam. 16. v. 15. Nam spiritus Iehoua recesserat à Saule, perturbat eum spiritus malus à Iehoua. Confer cap. 18. vers. 10. & 19. vers. 9.35

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "ips[?]um" (a blot over the letters before "um" in the first line); the Greek "ὁ πειράζων" is marked [?] because the scan is faint at that word. The printed number 312 is at top left. Marginal numbers 5 to 35 are line markers in the right margin and are given as notes. The running head is "TRIUMPHUS". The last line "Iob.1." is taken as the catchword.
